# Niagara and material pitfalls

Behavior observed while building this project's VFX library on UE 5.8. Read it together with the [Niagara section](unreal-mcp-asset-authoring.md#niagara-systems) of the MCP workflow before authoring Niagara systems, FX materials, or GameplayCue effects. The look and performance rules stay in `docs/vfx-roadmap.md`. Correct this file in the same PR when a finding no longer holds.

## Compile state

- Replacing an input with Float From Curve and then setting the curve keys compiles the empty curve, so particles read 0. `GetSystemCompileState` still says UpToDate, and toggling `SetModuleEnabled` does not help. `EditorAppToolset.OpenEditorForAsset` recompiles; then save and close it with `AssetEditorSubsystem.close_all_editors_for_asset`.
- `SetSystemData` on an existing system starts no compile, so `GetStackIssues` and `GetSystemCompileState` time out after 120 s. Open the system, check and save it, then close the asset editor.
- After an editor restart, a compiled CPU emitter can render its defaults (for example white) although its expression is fine. Close the asset editor before `save_asset`, then `reload_packages` and dump the particle data once to confirm.
- Never build while Simulate or PIE runs. The builder also never resets `SimTarget` to CPU, so a GPU experiment sticks until you set it back.
- `CreateNiagaraSystem` from a template keeps the template's emitters with their modules (ShapeLocation, Gravity, Drag, scale modules), and an emitter of the same name is not reset. Remove template emitters with `RemoveEmitter` (`emitterToRemove`) and build from the Minimal template.
- The first Simulate after an editor restart renders decals as black boxes and skips some materials while shaders compile; wait a minute before judging the look.
- `TemplateSpecification` cannot be set through the tools.
- Never delete and recreate a half-built in-memory asset: `EditorAssetLibrary.delete_asset` on one raised a ForceDeleteObjects ensure plus a modal that froze MCP. Edit the asset instead.

## Stack inputs and HLSL

- `AddSetParametersModule` plus `SetStackInputData` with `NiagaraExt_StackInputData_HlslExpression` writes any attribute from a one-line expression; ternaries, `mul`, and `normalize` work on CPU and GPU emitters. Entries of one SetParameters module read the values from before the module, so chain modules for dependent values. A failed expression silently writes the entry's default value.
- VectorVM `frac` keeps the sign (`x - trunc(x)`); hash with `frac(abs(sin(x) * 43758.5453))`.
- Deterministic per-instance data: sibling emitters can share per-instance paths by hashing `floor(UniqueID / N)` with a user parameter. UniqueIDs start at 0 for a burst on a fresh or reset emitter.
- ShapeLocation "Offset Coordinate Space" and Initialize Particle "Position Offset Coordinate Space" default to Simulation, which is world space for world-space emitters; set Local for owner-relative offsets.
- Axis Angle rotation with Scale/Offset/Rotate did not rotate around the expected local axis. To sweep spawn positions, attach the system to a component the owner rotates.
- VortexVelocity is deprecated, and VortexForce is constant-magnitude, so a blade line bends.
- Loop Behavior and Loop Duration stay hidden (`SetStackInputData` refuses them) until Life Cycle Mode is Self (`/Niagara/Enums/ENiagaraEmitterLifeCycleMode`). Loop Duration accepts an HLSL expression such as `User.LandingTime + 1.9`.
- Attribute trimming failures look random: modules fall back to defaults, particles vanish, or decals show before their delay. Dump the particle data early instead of bisecting colours.
- Local-space flames from a world velocity: `mul(float4(-Engine.Owner.Velocity, 0), Engine.Owner.SystemWorldToLocalNoScale).xyz` gives the backward direction regardless of the carrier's rotation. World-space trails spread a frame's particles along `Engine.Owner.Position - Engine.Owner.Velocity * Engine.DeltaTime * rand`.
- Orbit-then-release without a solver: integrate angle, radius, and height in one SetParameters module; in the next, set the velocity from the orbit position delta while orbiting, and the position from the orbit or from the last velocity (both read the old values), so the release keeps the last orbit velocity.
- Spawn per distance: an HLSL expression on SpawnRate such as `length(Engine.Owner.Velocity) / spacing` lays tracks.
- Steady pulsed lights or glows: spawn rate R with lifetime 2/R and intensity sin²(π · NormalizedAge) keeps the sum constant and still dies within 2/R after Deactivate.

## Renderers

- A light renderer without a `LightRadius` attribute uses 100 cm × `RadiusScale`, so the Light_Attributes module is unnecessary.
- SubUV: set Define SubUV Setup Manually to Manual (8 × 8); no renderer-info data interface is needed.
- The ribbon renderer binds `Particles.RibbonID` as `NiagaraID` by default; an int32 attribute of that name is ignored, and all points join one ribbon. `bLinkOrderUseUniqueID` is not settable; write `Particles.RibbonLinkOrder`. Branches can run as out-and-back excursions with link orders between the fork and the next main point.
- GPU ribbons work with HLSL SetParameters; two emitters with identical hashes give a core and a halo.
- The decal renderer projects down by default. `Particles.DecalSize` is a full-size vector (X is the projection depth), and `Particles.DecalFade` drives `DecalLifetimeOpacity`. A down-projecting decal with random yaw `a` is `float4(-0.7071*sin(a), 0.7071*cos(a), 0.7071*sin(a), 0.7071*cos(a))`.
- One-sided custom-facing sprites are culled from behind; emit pairs facing +X and -X.

## Scalability and culling

- An Effect Type with `bCullWhenNotRendered` culls looping effects that are legitimately empty (spawn rate 0), and they never resume. `FXT_Gameplay_Looping` has it off.
- Effect Types pre-cull spawns by frustum, instance budget, and distance, and the spawn call then returns None. Every Blueprint that sets user parameters on the result needs `IsValid`. `FXT_Gameplay_Burst` also kills a running burst the moment it leaves the frustum.
- Critical or long-lived bursts and big looping effects need a system scalability override: `SetSystemData` with `bOverrideScalabilitySettings=True` and `SystemScalabilityOverrides` for all platforms (quality level mask 31) that override visibility culling and, where needed, distance and instance-count settings. A looping cue spawns once, so a pre-cull refusal would hide it for its whole life.
- Effect Type spawn scaling (`FXT_Gameplay_Burst` scales Low by 0.5) also halves ribbon points. Override it per emitter with `ScalabilityOverrides` (`bOverrideSpawnCountScale`, `bScaleSpawnCount`, `SpawnCountScale` 1) through `SetEmitterData`.
- The engine refraction pass costs about 0.9 ms whenever a heat-haze sprite is on screen; gate haze emitters to High and above.

## Materials

- The project renders with Substrate. A refraction material with opacity 0 needs `refraction_coverage_mode = RCM_COVERAGE_IGNORED`, or the offset vanishes.
- Emissive FX are invisible under the test maps' manual daylight exposure unless they are exposure-relative: `MPC_FX_Exposure` mix 1 plus `MF_FX_ExposureCompensation`.
- `MaterialEditingLibrary.set_material_instance_*` returns False even on success; read the value back. Static switch changes need `recompile_material(base)`.
- Reparenting a material instance with `set_material_instance_parent` drops its static switch overrides. Record every switch with `get_material_instance_static_switch_parameter_value` first and set them again afterwards.
- `M_FX_SmokeAndFire` emits only with its static switch Use Emissive Color on. `MI_FX_SmokePuff` and `MI_FX_SmokeWispy` have it off, so an emissive gain does nothing there; `MI_FX_FireRoil` and `MI_FX_FlameWispy` have it on.
- Blackbody brightness scales with (T / 2500 K)⁴: about 3000 K with gain 20-30 reads as orange fire, 5000 K as white, about 1300 K as black. Fire sprites need a near-black particle colour, because it is lit base colour, or they read as sunlit puffs.
- Exposure-compensated `M_FX_Additive` in daylight: colour gain 0.5-4 reads orange, from about 8 yellow-white, and below 0.25 it is barely visible.
- `M_FX_DecalSubUV` is the Niagara Examples decal master.
- `MaterialEditingLibrary.get_input_node_output_name_for_material_expression` dereferenced null and crashed the editor. Dump material wiring with `get_inputs_for_material_expression` and `get_material_expression_input_names` only.

## Debugging and capture

- Check particle data with the console variable `fx.DumpParticleData 1`, set `0` in the next MCP call, and read the log. It also dumps an open Niagara editor's preview, and the lines of parallel emitters interleave, so close the asset editor first and match particles by attribute values. Count particles as spawn rate × lifetime, not from the dump.
- Run `fx.DumpNiagaraScalabilityState` and `fx.Niagara.DumpComponents` on the game world from `exec_python`. The component dump lists components per world with their execution and emitter states ("Free In Component Pool" means finished); read the log with `f.seek(byte_offset)`, not a character slice.
- Fast effects: use `slomo 0.1` in Simulate, or single timed captures across several runs. `slomo` from a separate MCP call lands 1-2 s after StartPIE, so trigger the effect in the same Python call and count frame times from there.
- `CaptureViewport` needs both `captureTransform` (`null` for the live viewport) and `annotations` (all zeros), returns the PNG as base64 in `returnValue.image.data`, and shows the editor camera during real PIE. In Simulate, move the camera first with `EditorAppToolset.SetCameraTransform`, which takes `location`; `translation` silently puts the camera at the origin.
- `ProfileGPU` with an unfocused editor profiles a Slate-only frame of about 1 ms. Call `CaptureViewport` right after it so the profiled frame renders the scene, set `r.ProfileGPU.ShowUI 0` to suppress the visualizer, and read `Translucency`, `Lights`, `Decals`, and `Niagara GPU Ribbons` under the second `SceneRender - ViewFamilies`. Pass names sit in the second-to-last `┃` cell; set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` when printing them on Windows.
- Pale smoke is invisible against the bright test sky.
- Python `set_actor_rotation` on a placed actor does not mark the map dirty, so the change is lost. Call `actor.modify()` first, then `EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_map(world, path)`. Changing a Blueprint component default does not move the component on placed instances; set the instance and save the map.

## Python and tool quirks

- `ObjectTools.set_properties` takes `values` as a JSON string; passing an object returns false with no change.
- `unreal.Rotator(a, b, c)` is (roll, pitch, yaw); pass keywords.
- `EditorValidatorSubsystem.validate_assets_with_settings(assets, settings)` returns a tuple.
- `GameplayCueParameters.location` needs an `unreal.Vector_NetQuantize10`. Build a tag with `tag = unreal.GameplayTag(); tag.import_text('(TagName="...")')`.
- `CreateNiagaraSystem` with an existing project system as `templateSystem` copies its emitters with their SetParameters expressions. To reuse one emitter, remove the others with `RemoveEmitter` and rewrite its entries with `SetStackInputData`, struct `/Script/NiagaraEditor.NiagaraExt_StackInputData_HlslExpression`, `inputNameStack` the entry name such as `Particles.Velocity`; remove user variables the new expressions no longer read (HRW-04b tool chips from the Rift Grip debris).
- A burst notify spawns its particle systems at the cue's `Location`, rotated to `Normal.Rotation()` unless the placement overrides the rotation, so `Engine.Owner.SystemXAxis` is the impact normal in a world-space emitter (HRW-04b).
- `CreateCueNotifyAsset` makes only Static or Actor notifies; reparent to `GameplayCueNotify_Burst` with `set_parent`. `GetCueInfo` and `FindCueNotifyAssets` do not see GameFeature cue paths.
- `GameplayCueNotify_Looping` with `AttachToTarget` plus `SnapToTarget` applied the target's world location again as a relative offset; use `KeepWorld`. Its particle and sound info structs are EditDefaultsOnly, so build the whole effects struct with `import_text` and assign it.
- Exporting flipbooks with `TextureExporterTGA` asserted and killed the editor; export PNG or EXR headlessly as [Asset library migration](asset-library-migration.md) describes.
